intent: Teach continuation_lines() that a line holding only a group's closing brace plus an operator (`} |`, `} >>file`) is not a statement, so kcov stops inflating the denominator with it. This is defect (a) in docs/kcov-under-report.md, in the flavour that caps four fixes/lib libs.
scope: python_pkg/tests/test_shell_coverage_lines.py (four new cases: two positive, two negative)
Non-goal: the backslash-continued ASSIGNMENT flavour that caps bt_adapter.sh line 97 -- it needs a command-vs-assignment distinction and is one line in one lib
Non-goal: clearing any lib from meta/shell-coverage-allowlist.txt, which follows in its own commit once each is re-measured
changes: Added _CLOSING_BRACE_OP = ^\s*\}\s*(\||>>?|<|&>) and one branch in continuation_lines() that excludes matching lines when no quote is open.

Anchoring on a LEADING closing brace is what makes this safe. bash attributes each command inside a group to its own line, and a pipe's right-hand side to its own line, so the brace-plus-operator line is left with no statement. A one-liner `{ echo a; } >file` starts with `{` and does not match; a bare `}` closing a function carries no operator and does not match.

Added four tests: `} |` and `} >>"$REPORT_FILE"` are continuations; a bare `}` closing a function and a single-line `{ echo a; } >"$out"` are NOT. The negative pair is the important half, because over-detection shrinks the denominator and INFLATES coverage -- the fail-open direction this test module's own header calls out.

verification.evidence: 18 passed. shell_coverage_lines.py: 56 statements, 40 branches, 0 missed, 0 partial = 100% -- so the new branch is covered in both directions, as the repo's fail_under=100 branch gate requires.

risks: A denominator change touches every measured lib, which is why it lands alone. The arithmetic bounds the blast radius: _measure computes denominator = kcov's line set minus excluded, and covered_set = (executed | traced) & denominator, so for any lib already at 100.00% the covered set IS the denominator and removing a subset leaves it at 100.00%. The five gated pacman_hook_stall libs, bt_report and bt_pairing therefore cannot regress, which the measurements above confirm for the two that were re-run.

The predicate is deliberately narrow. It does not cover `} &&`, `} ||` or a closing brace followed by a comment, and it does not touch the backslash-continued assignment flavour. Each would need its own evidence that bash attributes no statement to the line.
rollback: git revert the commit; continuation_lines() returns to quote-state detection only and the four new tests go with it.
After rollback, re-measure bt_audio.sh and arch_perf_report.sh and expect them back at 96.97% and 98.33%; neither is on the allowlist-cleared list, so no gate breaks.
